review.reason: Most cases discriminate their planned regressions (cancellation via signal.aborted plus final cache, keep-open via named onClose mocks, percent-literal URL encoding, whitespace-tolerant DDL regexes, shutdown ordering/timer, real 204 json spy). Two explicitly claimed regressions survive: the TodosPage toggle notice cannot distinguish saved.completed from !todo.completed, and the isOverdue local-vs-UTC midnight case is non-discriminating when tests run in UTC or a timezone behind UTC.

findings.location: frontend/src/features/todos/TodosPage.test.tsx: it.each 'toggles a task with completed=%s by sending the opposite state (saved: %s)'
findings.claim: The case claims notices follow the saved result, not the clicked todo, and gives that regression as a reason for testing both directions. In both table rows saved.completed === !initial, so a notice driven by the clicked todo is indistinguishable.
findings.evidence: Counterexample: change TodosPage.toggle to notify(!todo.completed ? 'Another task complete. Well done!' : 'Task marked as active.'). Row 1 (initial=false, saved=true) still gets 'Another task complete...'. Row 2 (initial=true, saved=false) still gets 'Task marked as active.'. Both assertions pass even though the notice ignores the server result. Fix: add a row where saved.completed === initial, e.g. initial=false, saved=false, expecting 'Task marked as active.'.

findings.location: frontend/src/features/todos/utils/todos.test.ts: 'uses the local calendar date shortly after midnight (due %s)'
findings.claim: value.regression says using the UTC date instead of the local date would be caught near midnight. The test pins only local 00:30 and sets no TZ, so a UTC implementation passes wherever the offset is zero or negative, including typical UTC CI runners.
findings.evidence: setSystemTime(new Date(2026, 9, 16, 0, 30)). Counterexample: build localDate from getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate. With TZ=UTC that is 2026-10-16, the same as local, so due '2026-10-15' -> true and '2026-10-16' -> false, and both rows pass. With a negative offset (e.g. America/*), 00:30 local is 04:30Z on the same date, which also passes. Only positive offsets detect it. No TZ pin was supplied in the reviewed files. Fix: pin a non-UTC TZ, or add a 23:30 local case together with the 00:30 case so either offset sign is caught.
